transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, the metal-fabrication lab has been closed while we prepared a revised operating plan. We now have a draft plan on the table that proposes reopening the lab for up to 20 students with standard protective equipment, ordinary end-of-class cleanup, and Ms. Ortiz as the instructor. Before I make a decision on approval, I'd like to follow our normal pre-authorization routine and hear final input from the instructor, safety officer, nurse, and industry-partnership coordinator. Could each of you share any final information or concerns you have about this reopening plan?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety concern before any decision is made. I completed an airflow test on the lab's ventilation system this week, and the results show that the current ventilation can only support up to 12 students working in the booths at one time — not the 20 proposed in the draft plan. I submitted the test to maintenance, but it appears the revised operating-plan folder hasn't been updated with this finding yet. We should not approve reopening for 20 students based on this ventilation limitation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share a critical finding from my fire-code review, which I finalized this week. The review requires a hot-work permit for every lab session and a continuous 30-minute fire watch after welding ends. However, I should note that the approval packet still contains only the ordinary cleanup procedure and does not yet reflect these fire-code requirements.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag an important health concern before any decision is made. Two students registered for the lab have health plans requiring a powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) during welding. I confirmed both the health plans and the availability of two compatible PAPR units this week — the school does have the equipment on hand. However, I have not yet entered this requirement into the lab plan. The draft plan currently only references standard protective equipment, and it does not account for these PAPR requirements. This needs to be incorporated into the operating plan before reopening is approved.

The insurer's credential file, which I received confirmation on this week, shows that Ms. Ortiz's welding-instructor credential expired last month. The insurer authorizes reopening only with Mr. Bell — whose current credential is verified — serving as lead instructor on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
